title: docs(core): re-state the dataSource.filter note for the two populations the convergence split (objectui#8945)
body:
Fixes #8945

Clause-②: no

This PR re-states the `ElementDataSourceConfig` docblock in `@object-ui/core` for the two populations that the upstream `filter` convergence split apart. It changes comments and adds a patch changeset. No type, export, runtime behaviour or accepted set moves. Dispatched by the `domain:spec @ objectui` seat, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01VhxTqosz7wn54ahqyxgERT`.

## What changed

- `packages/core/src/data-scope/element-data-source.ts`, the `ElementDataSourceConfig` docblock. It said three shapes "legitimately reach a renderer here". It also typed `filter` as `unknown` "rather than the spec's `FilterCondition`". The docblock now separates two populations:
  - **What an author may write** is the `ViewFilterRule` array alone. `ElementDataSourceSchema` refuses the record form by kind. It refuses an AST tuple array at its first member, because each member must be a rule object.
  - **What a renderer may still receive** is all three shapes. Upstream's D2 conversion `page-component-filter-record-to-rule-array` rewrites a stored `filter` only where the rule array spells it losslessly (a flat record, an operator object whose operators the rule vocabulary spells, several such keys, or a single-level AST tuple array), on every ObjectStack stored-row read and under `os migrate meta --stored`. It leaves exactly as stored a filter carrying `$and` / `$or` / `$not`, any filter with a part that has no lossless rule spelling, and every filter of a component whose rows are inline. This renderer is backend-agnostic and replays no conversion itself, so all three shapes may still arrive, and `mergeFilterNodes` still lowers each shape. *(Corrected in round 3 at `a9dd51ca0`, answering contract review `5921608196` ①-8.)*
  - The `unknown` type stays, and so does its reason: narrowing the type would only move the cast. The spec's type is now named `ViewFilterRule[]`, not `FilterCondition`.
- The same file's module docblock has an example binding that wrote `"filter": { … }`, which is the record form. It now writes `"filter": [ … ]`. This is a bounded in-place fix outside the docblock the claim named. See "File surface" below.
- `.changeset/8945-element-datasource-filter-note.md` adds a patch changeset for `@object-ui/core`.

## Premises, measured on this worktree's install

The install is `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0, and the branch is based on `e420df310`.

- **H1 holds.** The card's `Restart-when:` probe, run as written from the worktree root, exits **0**. Its controls are inside the predicate, so a dark instrument would have exited 9. A wider `ElementDataSourceSchema.safeParse` reading:
  - `{object}` is ACCEPTED. This is a control.
  - An unknown key is REFUSED with `unrecognized_keys`. This is a control.
  - The record form `{ status: 'open' }` is REFUSED with `invalid_type` at `filter`, expected an array.
  - The operator-object record `{ amount: { $gt: 5 } }` is REFUSED the same way.
  - The rule array `[{ field, operator, value }]` is ACCEPTED.
  - The AST tuple array `[['status','=','open']]` is REFUSED with `invalid_type` at `filter.0`, expected an object.
- **H2 holds.** The docblock still read 「three shapes legitimately reach a renderer here」 at `e420df310`. The installed `.d.ts` declares `filter` as an optional array of `ViewFilterRule` objects, and the spec's own `describe()` text for the key names the rule array and says the record form is refused.
- **H3 holds, so `record-picker.tsx` is untouched.** I read the three sites the card named, at the card's pin and on `main`:
  - The binding-composition comment carries no shape claim.
  - The comment saying the `filter` input is DECLARED carries no shape claim.
  - The registration's `filter` input was the site that described `FilterCondition` at the pin. It now declares `type: 'array'` and a rule-array description.
  - I checked that description against `ElementRecordPickerPropsSchema` on 17.5.0. The rule array is ACCEPTED. The record form and `$and` record are REFUSED at `filter`, expected an array. A tuple member is REFUSED at `filter.0`. The controls are `{object}`, ACCEPTED, and an unknown key, REFUSED. No sentence there misstates the door.

## File surface

The claim's surface is the `ElementDataSourceConfig` docblock, a `record-picker.tsx` sentence only if one still misstates the door, and one patch changeset. The diff also touches **one token in the same file's module docblock**: the example binding's `"filter": { … }` becomes `[ … ]`. All four bounded-fix conditions hold:
1. It is the same defect class, prose teaching the retired authoring shape.
2. It is a mechanical change, and the spec pins the target shape.
3. The claim reports that no other claim holds this file.
4. It is the same file and the same gates.

Leaving the example as it was would have made the file contradict its own re-stated note. The seat owes a same-round addition of this site to the claim's file surface.

## Author population: the card's open measurement

This is a historical reading at HEAD `4837c74e6` on spec 17.5.0. Nothing re-derives it.

**Method.** It parses candidates, and no regex is involved.
1. Enumerate tracked files from `git ls-tree -r HEAD` with a clean-tree assertion. That gives 6742 `.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs/.mts/.cts/.json` files; all 6742 parsed and 0 failed.
2. Walk the TypeScript AST for every object literal that is the value of a `dataSource` property, a `dataSource={{…}}` JSX attribute, or an `X.dataSource =` assignment, and that carries a `filter` key.
3. Evaluate the literal statically.
4. Judge each candidate with the installed `ElementDataSourceSchema.safeParse` three times: on the value with `filter` removed, which decides whether it is a binding at all; on the full value; and on `filter` alone.

The instrument controls, rule array ACCEPTED and record REFUSED, are lit. A positive control is also lit: the eight fixtures listed on objectui#11117 were all found, 8 of 8.

**Reading.** There are 36 candidates, all in test sources and none in non-test source.
- 6 bindings already write the rule array and parse clean.
- **24 bindings write a retired orthography across 18 test files: 19 AST tuple arrays and 5 records.**
- 1 rule array is refused for its value shape: an `equals` with an array comparand. It is a deliberate objectui#8557 fixture, not an orthography author.
- 4 have a non-static `filter` and were not measured.
- 1 is not a binding: its other keys fail, with `invalid_type` at `object`, deliberately.

`.md` and `.mdx` fences are outside this instrument; they belong to objectui#11117.

The upstream entry's "seventeen (fifteen tuple arrays, two records)" was taken at a different pin. It is not comparable, and this PR does not assert a rival reading of it.

## Patch round 2, at HEAD `0b4445d5a` (written by the seat)

- `.changeset/7297-record-id-filter-token.md` gains a dated correction, append-only (`+2/−0`), with frontmatter md5 `2935e1e656cbeb29b6093519d07dde85` before and after.
  - Its record-form `element:number` filter example `{ "assignee": "{record_id}" }` is refused on `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 (`invalid_type` at `filter`, expected array).
  - The note gives the accepted `ViewFilterRule` array, `[{ "field": "assignee", "operator": "equals", "value": "{record_id}" }]`. It was measured with `ElementNumberPropsSchema.safeParse` and `ElementDataSourceSchema.safeParse` before writing, with both controls lit.
- This is a bounded in-place fix the seat requested, because the text is release-bound (release PR #5400 is open). The claim's file surface was amended in the same round: objectui#8945 comment `5921413381`.
- Gates at `0b4445d5a`: `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:control-bytes` and `check:new-line-citations` each exit 0. No package source changed since `4837c74e6`, so round 1's `@object-ui/core` build, type-check, test and lint still stand.

## Acceptance notes

- objectui#11117 is not addressed here. Its listed fixture population, eight fixtures in six files, is a subset of the 24 above. Some of those fixtures pin how a renderer handles **stored** legacy shapes, for example the objectui#10789 malformed-filter pins. Those fixtures belong to the renderer population this note now names, so converting them all to the rule array could delete legitimate coverage. That judgement is objectui#11117's to make.
- objectui#8220 is not addressed here.
- The `toFilterNode` doc in `packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts` says "three shapes in circulation, all legitimate" about what a view hands a renderer. That statement is about the renderer population and stays accurate, so it is not edited.
- `record-picker.tsx` is unchanged because H3 held.
